title: Hand rankings
summary: Which hand beats which, kickers, the wheel and split pots.

intro.text: A hand is always **five cards**. Suits are equal: a spade flush is no better than a heart flush. Below are all the hands from strongest to weakest, with how often each one is made by the river from seven cards.

ranking.caption: The rarer the hand, the stronger it is.

kicker.text: When two players have the same kind of hand, the hands are compared by their highest cards, then by **kickers**: the cards that fill up the five without being part of the pair or set. A pair of aces with a king beats a pair of aces with a queen.

labels: Pair of aces, king kicker: wins

wheel.text: In a straight the ace can be the highest or the lowest card. **A-2-3-4-5** is the lowest straight, called the wheel. A straight can't wrap around the ace: Q-K-A-2-3 is not a straight.

ties.text:
How to compare hands of the same kind:
- **Flush**: by the highest card, then the next one.
- **Full house**: by the three of a kind first, then the pair: aces full of kings beat kings full of aces.
- **Two pair**: by the higher pair, then the lower one, then the kicker.
- If the five cards are exactly equal, the pot is **split**.

q-flush.q: Which is stronger, a straight or a flush?
q-flush.explain: A flush beats a straight: it comes less often (about 3% against 4.6% by the river).

q-board-pairs.q: Board: Kh Kd 7c 7s 2h. You hold A3, your opponent Q8. Who wins?
q-board-pairs.explain: Both have two pair, kings and sevens from the board. The fifth card is the kicker: your ace beats their queen.

t1.q: Which is higher, a full house or a flush?
t1.explain: A full house (three of a kind plus a pair) beats a flush.

t2.explain: The ace can play low in a straight: A-2-3-4-5 is the wheel, the lowest straight.

t3.q: The board is Ah Kh Qh Jh Th. You have 2c 2d, your opponent As Ks. Who wins?
t3.explain: The board is a royal flush, nothing can beat it. Both players play the board: the pot is split.

t4.q: How many cards make a hand?
t4.explain: From the seven cards available (two in your hand, five on the board) you pick the best five.
